en: The Ritual Manual for the Yoga of the Syllable-Wheels of the Dharmakāya of Vairocana, for the Immediate Realization of the "Entering the Dharma Realm" Chapter of the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha’s Great Vaipulya*. Now,
for those who wish to enter immediately into the One Vehicle and practice the contemplation of the Dharmakāya of the Tathāgata Vairocana:
First, one should give rise to the subtle vows and practices of Samantabhadra Bodhisattva.
Furthermore, one should empower the body and mind through the three secrets;
thus, one will be able to awaken into and enter the great ocean of Mañjuśrī’s wisdom.
However, at the outset, the practitioner, in a secluded place,
collects the mind and settles it, closes the eyes, straightens the body, and sits in the full lotus posture.
They direct the mind to universally encompass the boundless ocean of lands.
Contemplate clearly that all Tathāgatas of the three periods of time are present before each and every Buddha and Bodhisattva,
reverently and diligently prostrating, circumambulating,
and offering oceans of clouds of various kinds of ritual implements.
Having performed such vast offerings to all these noble beings,
one should then contemplate one's own mind.
The mind is fundamentally unborn;
its self-nature is spontaneously accomplished,
and its luminosity shines everywhere like space.
Furthermore, one should give rise to profound compassion, thinking with pity:
"Sentient beings do not realize that their own minds revolve through the various realms of existence;
I shall universally transform them and deliver them."
One should cause them to attain awakening such that nothing remains unexhausted.
Furthermore, one should observe that one's own mind, the minds of all sentient beings,
and the minds of all Buddhas are fundamentally no different, being equal and of a single characteristic.
The great Bodhicitta is formed;
translucent, cool, and vast, it pervades everywhere.
Perfectly luminous and pure, it becomes a great lunar disc.
Its measure is equal to space and has no boundaries.
Furthermore, one should arrange the forty-two Brahma-syllables in a clockwise direction within the lunar disc.
All were entirely golden, emitting great radiance that illuminated and penetrated the ten directions, appearing with distinct clarity.
Within each ray of light, one beheld immeasurable oceans of lands.
There are immeasurable Buddhas,
surrounded before and behind by immeasurable assemblies,
seated at the site of enlightenment and having attained perfect awakening.
With wisdom that penetrates the three periods of time and a body that pervades the ten directions,
he turns the great wheel of Dharma to deliver all classes of beings,
causing them all to realize for themselves the nirvana of non-abiding.
Furthermore, one should enter the forty-two letter gates of the Prajñāpāramitā,
realizing that all phenomena are ultimately unapprehendable,
and being able to contemplate the dharma-realm as it is perceived by correct wisdom.
All are entirely equal, without difference or distinction.
If a practitioner of yoga can bring themselves into accord with this *svādhiṣṭhāna-dhāraṇī* through contemplative practice,
they will be able to directly realize the wisdom-body (*jñānakāya*) of the Tathāgata Vairocana.
Attaining non-obstruction regarding all phenomena,
the forty-two syllables of the Perfectly Radiant Wheel are chanted as follows:

A Ā RA LA VA TSA NA MA NA ŚA VA BHA YA ṢṬA KA SA MA GA THA JA ŚA VADHA ŚA KHA KṢA SVA NYA RTHA BHASA SMA HA VADHA TSA GHA CHA ÑA PHA ŚA KYA ŚA ŚCA ṬA ṬHA The Forty-Two Syllable Contemplation Gate from the "Entering the Dharma Realm" Chapter of the *Avataṃsaka Sūtra*.
